title: Mitigate ingress deadzones and long-context tail regression across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
Multiple customer escalations (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported recurring high tail latency for long-context workloads during mixed-request bursts. Problem manifests as intermittent "ingress deadzones": short windows where low-latency short requests are starved while long-sequence requests monopolize batch formation, producing 95/99th percentile regressions and customer timeouts.

Observed symptoms:
- Dedicated customer (ACME Financial) saw 99th percentile generation latency increase from 180ms -> 1.2s under typical daytime traffic that mixes short completions (<=32 tokens) with long-streaming sessions (>8192 tokens).
- Hosted API logs show bursts where a small number of long requests cause adaptive admission to hold new requests for >200ms despite GPU not being fully utilized.
- Private (on-prem) customer reported similar behavior when their autoscaler temporarily reduced worker count: long contexts amplified backlog and prevented short flows from being dequeued.

Initial analysis / root-cause hypothesis:
- Scheduler admission/queuing logic currently prioritizes throughput by waiting for size-matching batches; when long contexts are present the batcher extends wait windows to reach batch capacity, creating deadzones for short requests.
- Interaction with the preload/kv-cache eviction path: long-context requests perform heavy KV writes/churn which increases dequeue latencies for other tenants in the same worker.
- A regression in the adaptive-floodgate heuristic (recent change in runtime-1.18) mis-estimates the expected completion time for mixed-length windows, raising per-batch timers above safe thresholds.

Workplan / proposed fixes (phased):
1) Short-term hotpatch (<=72h):
   - Add an ingress age cap: requests older than X ms are forced into immediate dequeue (configurable per deployment).
   - Lower the adaptive-floodgate max-wait default for hosted tier to 30ms while we validate.
   - Add a per-tenant KV churn counter metric and an alert when eviction rate > threshold.
   - Rollout: hotpatch to Hosted first (canary 5% of traffic), Dedicated customers on request, Private customers via patch bundle.

2) Medium-term changes (2-4 weeks):
   - Implement age-prioritized dequeue: maintain a compact priority wheel that favors older short requests while still allowing long batches to progress.
   - Introduce per-workload batch size target (learned from telemetry) so mixers don't apply uniform thresholds across heterogeneous traffic.
   - Isolate KV eviction IO paths from dispatch thread to avoid dequeue pauses during heavy KV operations.

3) Long-term (quarter):
   - Add synthetic e2e replay tests to CI that simulate mixed-length tenant traffic at scale and assert 95/99 p99 bounds.
   - Contribute runtime admission policy that is topology-aware (separately tune hosted/dedicated/private defaults).

Monitoring and acceptance criteria:
- New metrics: batcher_age_p90, per_tenant_kv_eviction_rate, forced_dequeue_count.
- SLA targets: 95th percentile latency for short requests (<=32 tokens) must remain < 250ms under the customer workload profile used in the ACME repro.
- Canary rollout pass defined as no customer-impacting alerts and stable host GPU utilization across 48h window.

Rollout plan / risk mitigation:
- Hotpatch will be feature-flagged; ops can flip to previous behavior within 5m.
- Canary 5% hosted -> 25% hosted -> all hosted. Dedicated customers who reported incidents will be manually enrolled into canary if they opt-in. Private customers will receive a patch bundle and doc with rollback instructions.
